text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to a specific URL. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access the data, you usually need authentication, often using an API key or a token. Be careful with rate limits, because sending too many requests can temporarily block your access. Finally, always include error handling in your code. Check the status codes and prepare for failures, so your application stays stable and reliable.
